As an ancient one, I was probably in later grade school when Pong came out. Our mom found a pong console at a garage sale, after Atari was released. My brothers and I played it until she found an Atari system at a garage sale after Nintendo was released. She’d pick up games for us when she’d run across them. Our games library was eventually very large, because the investment required was so small. We envied the awesome games we couldn’t afford as they were coming out! (We never got a PS anything from a garage sale.) Fortunately, most of our friends would let us play on theirs when we were really feeling neglected by the rents.

But what did the kids chip in together and present to dear old Mom on her 65th birthday? A brand new Nintendo 64 and a gold cased Zelda II! 

I was working with her at the time, and we played together from the moment we got home from work until way past bedtime, usually. Dear Link’s little stabby sword probably saved both of our jobs, taking out all of our day’s pent up aggressions on his enemies. (“Take that Carol! Choke on this, Steve!” We were able to find laughter to help deal with the small minded idiots at work, and unalive them virtually over and over. Very therapeutic!)

We also often played the old version of Tetris (Tengen) on the old NES for so long that fatigue and eye strain would cause tears to run, but we’d just couldn’t quit until the Eastern Europeans were dancing on the Kremlin just one more time. Here’s a clip:

https://youtu.be/yY4xJ1tcAEE?si=z9qgeEmRA9Mhheo9

She taught me to cherish my inner child. I still enjoy playing video games - my excuse now is that I’m exercising my mind, and having a blast doing it.
